REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
AND SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
ZOOM VIDEO COMMUNICATIONS, MEETING ID # 823 8342 5689
LEGISLATIVE BODY MEMBERS MAY PARTICIPATE FROM THE COUNCIL CHAMBER, 18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, OR VIA TELECONFERENCE AUTHORIZED BY STATE OF CALIFORNIA EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20 AND N-29-20
* THE CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER REMAINS CLOSED TO THE PUBLIC *
INSTRUCTIONS FOR PUBLIC PARTICIPATION IN THIS MEETING ARE LISTED BELOW
THURSDAY - DECEMBER 10, 2020 -
07:00 P.M.
*COVID-19 NOTICE*
To protect public health and safety during the local, state, and federally declared COVID-19 emergency, and in compliance with the current Los Angeles County Health Officer Order, the City Council Chamber remains closed to the public. As authorized by State of California Executive Orders N-25-20 and N-29-20 this meeting will be conducted via teleconference. Public observation and participation in this meeting will be facilitated through the methods described below.
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after the distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at 562-916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION:
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or by connecting to the ZOOM meeting described below.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting using any of the following methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Teleconference Participation: Live audio public comments can be made by connecting to the meeting using the information listed below. Public speakers will be queued to provide comment at the appropriate time during the meeting agenda and must be available at the time they are called upon to speak.
Cerritos Zoom meeting online link: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82383425689
Cerritos Zoom Meeting call-in telephone number: (669) 900-6833
Cerritos Zoom Meeting ID: 823 8342 5689
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations:
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the teleconference meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY AND A SPECIAL
MEETING OF THE CERRITOS PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY HELD DECEMBER 10,
2020, 7:00 P.M., IN HYBRID MODE FROM THE COUNCIL CHAMBER, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA AND VIA TELECONFERENCE AS AUTHORIZED BY
STATE OF CALIFORNIA EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20 AND N-29-20, VIA ZOOM VIDEO
COMMUNICATIONS, MEETING ID# 823 8342 5689

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Naresh Solanki.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency/Public Financing Authority
  were in attendance:

  Council/Agency/Authority Member Bruce Barrows
  Council/Agency/Authority Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency/Authority Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Chuong Vo
  Mayor/Chair Naresh Solanki

5.  Presentations/Appointments

  Proclamations were made by the City Council as follows:

  Marcella Kroupa McMahon (in honor of her 100th birthday celebration on November 10,
  2020).

  Mark Steres, City Attorney (in honor of his retirement after nearly 30 years of service to the
  City of Cerritos).

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Mark Steres, City Attorney, provided the following report from the November 23, 2020,
  7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Closed Session:

  The City Council met in Closed Session to discuss Items 12A and 12B as listed on the
  November 23, 2020, 7:00 p.m. agenda:

  12A. CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(4) (COUNCIL)
  Number of cases: One (1)

  12B. PUBLIC EMPLOYMENT
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957(b) (COUNCIL)
  Title: City Attorney
 City of Cerritos  December 10, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency/Public Financing Authority  Page 2 of 8

5.  Presentations/Appointments (continued)

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT (continued)

  With regard to Item 12A, the City Council discussed the item and there was no
  reportable action. With regard to Item 12B, the City Council discussed the item and
  there was no reportable action.

  This concluded the City Attorney’s report from the November 23, 2020, 7:00 p.m. City
  Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Written correspondence:
  (Written correspondence is considered public record and full-text copies of submitted
  written correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer.)

  Guy Bremer expressed concern regarding homeless encampments along the riverbed
  bike path under Artesia Boulevard.

  Audio public comments:

  Murali Vasudevan thanked the City Council for the Santa Sleigh Program and expressed
  concerns with the City’s new water billing system.

  Malik Tariq spoke regarding his religious faith as related to the COVID-19 pandemic.

  Noting there were no other individuals who provided written correspondence or elected
  to speak, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes of November 23,
  2020 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Hu, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes of November 23, 2020
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

(minutes continue on the next page)
 City of Cerritos  December 10, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency/Public Financing Authority  Page 3 of 8

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands

7B.1. Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated December 10, 2020
  (COUNCIL).

  This item was pulled from the Consent Calendar by Mayor Pro Tem Vo for separate
  consideration

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Barrows, to approve the Register of
  Demands, as follows, with the exception of Line Item 190795 (which was not approved):

  City of Cerritos  12/10/2020  $ 4,132,323.27 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Approval of Treasurer’s Reports

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending
  October 31, 2020 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Hu, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending October 31, 2020
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7D.  Waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  CERRITOS, SUPERSEDING RESOLUTION NO. 2020-18, APPROVING AND ATTESTING TO
  THE VERACITY OF THE 2019 POWER SOURCE DISCLOSURE ANNUAL REPORT AND
  POWER CONTENT LABEL TO THE CALIFORNIA ENERGY COMMISSION (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Hu, to waive full reading of and
  adopt Resolution 2020-33, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  CERRITOS, SUPERSEDING RESOLUTION NO. 2020-18, APPROVING AND
  ATTESTING TO THE VERACITY OF THE 2019 POWER SOURCE DISCLOSURE
  ANNUAL REPORT AND POWER CONTENT LABEL TO THE CALIFORNIA ENERGY
  COMMISSION (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7E.  Award of contract for Cerritos Library Chinese language book collection development
  services, RFP No. 1410-20 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Hu, to award a professional services
  contract for the Cerritos Library Chinese Language book collection development services to
  Multicultural Books and Videos, based on the company’s proposal, with a term of thirty-six
  (36) months with a provision for up to three (3) twelve (12) month extensions (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7F.  Award of contract for Cerritos Library Korean language book collection development
  services, RFP No. 1411-20 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Hu, to award a professional services
  contract for the Cerritos Library Korean Language book collection development services to
  Total Library Services, based on the company’s proposal, with a term of thirty-six (36)
  months with a provision for up to three (3) twelve (12) month extensions, and reject the
  other proposal (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7G.  Approval of the completion of the biennial review of the City of Cerritos and its
  subagencies’ conflict of interest codes pursuant to the Political Reform Act of 1974 by
  adoption of the following proposed resolution:

  Waive full reading of and adopt A JOINT RESOLUTION OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL,
  SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY, AND CERRITOS
  PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY ADOPTING THE AMENDED CONFLICT OF INTEREST
  CODES, AND REPEALING RESOLUTION NOS. 2018-21, SA 2018-04, AND CPFA 2018-01
  (COUNCIL/AGENCY/AUTHORITY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Hu, to approve the completion of the
  2020 biennial review of the City of Cerritos, Successor Agency to the Cerritos Redevelopment
  Agency, and Cerritos Public Financing Authority conflict of interest codes pursuant to the
  Political Reform Act of 1974 by waiving full reading of and adopting Joint Resolution Nos.
  2020-34, SA 2020-02, and CPFA 2020-01, A JOINT RESOLUTION OF THE
  CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL, SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS
  REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY, AND CERRITOS PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
  ADOPTING THE AMENDED CONFLICT OF INTEREST CODES, AND REPEALING
  RESOLUTION  NOS.  2018-21,  SA  2018-04,  AND  CPFA  2018-01
  (COUNCIL/AGENCY/AUTHORITY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  December 10, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency/Public Financing Authority  Page 5 of 8

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AUTHORIZING UTILIZATION OF RESTRICTED COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) FUNDS AS FOLLOWS: (1) $116,000 IN CARES
  ACT COVID-19 CDBG FUNDS TO MAKE COVID-19 PREVENTION AND ACCESSIBILITY
  RELATED IMPROVEMENTS AT THE CERRITOS SENIOR CENTER; (2) $187,000 IN FISCAL
  YEAR 2021-2022 CDBG FUNDS TO IMPROVE ACCESSIBILITY TO PLAYGROUND
  EQUIPMENT LOCATED AT ROSEWOOD PARK; AND (3) $219,000 IN SURPLUS CDBG
  FUNDS TO CONSTRUCT AND RETROFIT ACCESSIBLE CURB RAMPS AND MAKE
  NECESSARY SIDEWALK REPAIRS WITHIN THE CITY OF CERRITOS (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kristin Aguila, Advanced Planning/Economic Development
  Manager. A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments period. Noting there were no
  individuals who provided written correspondence or elected to speak, the Mayor declared
  the public comments period and public hearing closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to waive full reading of and
  adopt Resolution No. 2020-35, A RESOLUTION OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL
  AUTHORIZING UTILIZATION OF RESTRICTED COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT
  BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) FUNDS AS FOLLOWS: (1) $116,000 IN CARES ACT
  COVID-19 CDBG FUNDS TO MAKE COVID-19 PREVENTION AND ACCESSIBILITY
  RELATED IMPROVEMENTS AT THE CERRITOS SENIOR CENTER; (2) $187,000 IN
  FISCAL YEAR 2021-2022 CDBG FUNDS TO IMPROVE ACCESSIBILITY TO
  PLAYGROUND EQUIPMENT LOCATED AT ROSEWOOD PARK; AND (3) $219,000
  IN SURPLUS CDBG FUNDS TO CONSTRUCT AND RETROFIT ACCESSIBLE CURB
  RAMPS AND MAKE NECESSARY SIDEWALK REPAIRS WITHIN THE CITY OF
  CERRITOS (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of an informational update on the City's response to the
  COVID-19 local emergency (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Annie Hylton, City Librarian & Marketing Manager. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  provided written correspondence or elected to speak, the Mayor declared the public
  comments period closed.

  There was no further action taken on this item.

(minutes continue on the next page)
 City of Cerritos  December 10, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency/Public Financing Authority  Page 6 of 8

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  Review and consideration of award of contract for the City Hall roof replacement, Project
  No. 12704, Bid No. 1412-20 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  provided written correspondence or elected to speak, the Mayor declared the public
  comments period closed.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Manager to provide a copy of the previous
  report to the City Council regarding the costs to rehabilitate/replace the existing City
  Hall air conditioning/heating system and provide the current cost estimates for same
  prior to the consideration of the FY 2021-22 budget.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to:

  1. Award a contract in the amount of $550,000 for the City Hall Roof Replacement
  (total bid), Project No. 12704, Bid No. 1412-20, to Letner Roofing Company, and
  reject the other bids; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager to access the additional amounts necessary to complete
  Project No. 12704 from savings realized to date in the current fiscal year from the
  City’s operational budget; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project-related change
  orders (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9C.  Review and consideration of an informational update on the groundwater treatment
  station at the Civic Center parking structure (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Mike O’Grady, Environmental Services Manager. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  provided written correspondence or elected to speak, the Mayor declared the public
  comments period closed.

  The City Council unanimously received and filed this report. There was no further action
  taken on this item.

(minutes continue on the next page)
 City of Cerritos  December 10, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency/Public Financing Authority  Page 7 of 8

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9D.  Review and consideration of the proposed 2021 City Council/Successor Agency Regular
  and Special Meeting schedule (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer. A PowerPoint presentation
  was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  provided written correspondence or elected to speak, the Mayor declared the public
  comments period closed.

  This item was continued by unanimous consent of the City Council/Successor Agency to
  their January 14, 2021 Regular Meeting. There was no further action taken on this item.

9E.  Review and consideration of temporarily modifying the criteria governing the City’s
  overnight vehicle parking permit program and reestablishing street sweeping regulations
  (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Daryl Evans, Public Safety Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Eric Schulte expressed concerns with the criteria governing the City’s overnight vehicle
  parking permit program.

  Noting there were no other individuals who provided written correspondence or elected
  to speak, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Barrows, to:

  1. Amend the existing emergency order repealing the moratorium on the City’s parking
  enforcement, including overnight residential parking restrictions and street sweeping
  enforcement, and direct the City Manager to reinstitute the City’s parking
  enforcement program effective January 11, 2021, or within a reasonable timeframe
  thereafter, if necessary, to complete the administrative procedures related to
  reinstatement of the program and reinstatement of the appropriate number of
  parking control officers; and

  2. Amend permanently the existing parking permit criteria to allow households with five
  (5) vehicles and five (5) licensed drivers to qualify for a second annual parking
  permit. The same ratio would be applied toward homes with a three-car garage; and

  3. Temporarily allow all Cerritos residents and students with a driver’s license and
  vehicle to be issued a limited “Special Circumstance” parking permit which is valid
  for 90 days. This would allow parking enforcement officers to issue citations to
  unauthorized vehicles during the restricted hours of 3:00 a.m. until 5:00 a.m.
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  Yokoyama
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  December 10, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency/Public Financing Authority  Page 8 of 8

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation.

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Barrows, Hu, and Yokoyama, Mayor Pro Tem
  Vo, and Mayor Solanki.

  CONSENSUS (Vo): Directed the City Manager to research the feasibility of establishing
  a City Prosecutor to prosecute misdemeanor offenses in the City and provide a report to
  the City Council.

  CONSENSUS (Vo): Directed the City Manager to provide quarterly reports from the
  Cerritos Regional Chamber of Commerce as related to services provided to the business
  community.

12.  Closed Session

  City Attorney Mark Steres announced the City Council would recess to Closed Session to
  discuss the items listed on the Closed Session agenda. An announcement regarding any
  reportable action resulting from the Closed Session will be made at the next regular
  meeting.

12A.  PUBLIC EMPLOYMENT
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957(b) (COUNCIL)
  Title: City Attorney

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 11:17 p.m.

  /s/Vida Barone
  Vida Barone, City Clerk/Agency Secretary
